mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the time period (T) of an oscillation?

options.A: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.B: The number of oscillations per second.
options.D: The time taken to reach the equilibrium position from the extreme.

mcqs.answer: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
mcqs.explanation: The time period T is the duration of one full cycle of the motion. Option B describes frequency, not period. Option C is the definition of amplitude. Option D is only a part of the motion, not the full cycle.

mcqs.question: A simple pendulum makes 20 complete oscillations in 40 seconds. What is its frequency?
mcqs.explanation: Frequency f = number of oscillations / time = 20 / 40 = 0.5 s⁻¹ = 0.5 Hz. The other options result from incorrect inversion or misplacement of the numbers.

mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes periodic motion from non‑periodic motion?

options.A: Periodic motion repeats its pattern after a fixed time interval, whereas non‑periodic motion never repeats exactly.
options.B: Periodic motion occurs only in mechanical systems, while non‑periodic motion occurs only in electrical systems.
options.C: Periodic motion always has constant speed, while non‑periodic motion always has varying speed.
options.D: Periodic motion requires a restoring force, whereas non‑periodic motion does not.

mcqs.answer: Periodic motion repeats its pattern after a fixed time interval, whereas non‑periodic motion never repeats exactly.
mcqs.explanation: The defining feature of periodic motion is the repeatability after a definite period. Options B, C, and D introduce unrelated criteria that are not necessary for periodicity.

mcqs.question: Oscillatory motion can be best described as:

options.A: A motion in which an object moves back and forth about a fixed equilibrium position.
options.B: A motion in which an object moves in a straight line with constant velocity.
options.C: A motion that occurs only in rotating systems.
options.D: A motion where the displacement increases indefinitely with time.

mcqs.answer: A motion in which an object moves back and forth about a fixed equilibrium position.
mcqs.explanation: Oscillatory motion involves repeated displacement about an equilibrium point. Option B describes uniform linear motion, C is too restrictive, and D describes unbounded motion, not oscillation.

mcqs.question: In the motion of a simple pendulum, the point at which the net restoring force is zero is called the:
mcqs.explanation: When the pendulum passes through the vertical line, the gravitational component providing the restoring force vanishes; this is the equilibrium position. The maximum displacement point and turning point refer to the extreme positions, while amplitude is the magnitude of that displacement.

mcqs.question: Amplitude of an oscillation is defined as:

options.A: The total distance traveled in one complete cycle.
options.B: The maximum displacement of the system from its equilibrium position.
options.C: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.D: The number of oscillations per second.

mcqs.answer: The maximum displacement of the system from its equilibrium position.
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude measures how far the system moves away from equilibrium at its extreme. Option A describes the path length, C is the period, and D is frequency.

mcqs.question: How does the time period (T) of an oscillation differ from its frequency (f)?

options.A: T is the number of oscillations per second, while f is the time for one oscillation.
options.B: T is measured in seconds and represents the time for one complete oscillation, whereas f is measured in hertz and represents the number of oscillations per second.
options.C: Both T and f have the same units and represent the same quantity.
options.D: T is the maximum displacement, while f is the speed of oscillation.

mcqs.answer: T is measured in seconds and represents the time for one complete oscillation, whereas f is measured in hertz and represents the number of oscillations per second.
mcqs.explanation: Period (T) and frequency (f) are reciprocal quantities: T = 1/f. T has units of seconds, f has units of hertz (s⁻¹). The other options invert or confuse the definitions.

mcqs.question: A mass‑spring system has a time period of 0.5 s. What is its frequency?
mcqs.explanation: Frequency f = 1 / T = 1 / 0.5 s = 2 s⁻¹ = 2 Hz. Option A mistakenly treats period as frequency, while C and D are incorrect values.
